title: One quantity as a percentage of another
log: 2026-11-20T12:15:19Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points teaches finding what percentage one quantity is of another (part over whole, then times 100); they cover finding a percentage of an amount, converting fractions to percentages, and increases or discounts.

draft.title: One quantity as a percentage of another
card: To write one quantity as a percentage of another, put the part over the whole as a fraction. The whole is the amount you are comparing against.
Both amounts must be in the same units. Change one first if they are not, such as metres to centimetres.
Multiply the fraction by 100 to get the percentage: \(\frac{\text{part}}{\text{whole}} \times 100\).
Example: 18 of 24 students walk to school. \(\frac{18}{24} \times 100 = 75\), so \(75\%\) walk.
draft.remember: Part over whole, in the same units, then times 100.

a.q: Jack saves $30 of the $120 he earns. What percentage of his earnings does he save?
a.why: The part is 30 and the whole is 120, so \(\frac{30}{120} \times 100 = 25\%\). The answer \(400\%\) comes from putting the whole over the part.

b.q: A ribbon is 2 m long. Priya cuts off a piece 50 cm long. What percentage of the ribbon is the piece?
b.why: Change 2 m to 200 cm first, so the units match. Then \(\frac{50}{200} \times 100 = 25\%\). Using \(\frac{50}{100}\) gives \(50\%\), which ignores that the ribbon is 200 cm long.
